sentences.text: Author: Parth Prateem Sahu
Bench: Parth Prateem Sahu  1  NAFR  HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH, BILASPUR
MCRC No. 8801 of 2023 1- Hariram Gavde S/o Late Manauram Gavde Aged About 20 Years, R/o Village Banjoda, Uparpara, P.S. Dhanora, District- Kondagaon, Chhattisgarh.

---- Applicant  Versus 1- State Of Chhattisgarh, Through The Police Station Dhanora,
District- Kondagaon, Chhattisgarh.

---- Respondent For Applicant : Mr. P.K. Tulsyan, Advocate For Respondent/State : Mr. Neeraj Sharma, Dy.A.G.
Hon'ble Shri Justice Parth Prateem Sahu Order On Board 15/02/2024 1.

Applicant has filed this bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 for grant of regular bail as he has been arrested in connection with Crime No.48/2023,
registered at Police Station - Dhanora, District - Kondagaon (C.G.) for offence punishable under Section 376 (2) (n) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 6 of POCSO Act.
2. Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that applicant abducted the victim and has committed sexual intercourse with her.
Based on the report, aforementioned crime was registered and applicant was arrested.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
He has not committed any offence as alleged.

He contended that victim is major girl and after attaining majority, she with her own will performed marriage with applicant and is residing in his house and from their wedlock, they have been blessed with child.

During the trial victim and her mother were examined before the trial Court and victim stated that she is aged about 19 years and mother of victim also stated that victim delivered a child and she is residing in the house of applicant.
Hence, applicant may be released on bail.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for State opposes the submission of learned counsel for applicant, and would submit that serious allegations are levelled against applicant, however, he submits that deposition which is relied upon by learned counsel for applicant is subject matter of appreciation by learned trial Court.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

6. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances, nature of allegation as also the fact that victim and her mother have already been examined before the trial Court and they have not supported the case of the prosecution, without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am inclined to allow this bail application.
7. Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on regular bail upon his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court below on the conditions that:-
a). Applicant shall appear before the trial Court regularly on each and every date,
unless exempted from appearance.
(b). Applicant shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c). If the applicant is found involved in similar offence in the future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of Bail.
Certified copy as per rules.
